title: Choose Katedrala's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Construction Grid. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Construction Grid
options.lineage: International Typographic Style: Müller-Brockmann's grid systems
options.thesis: The page is a construction grid: every part of the architecture sits on one module, and order becomes visible the moment things lock to it.
materials: a visible 12-column construction grid on a baseline module
flush-left neo-grotesk at dramatic scale contrasts
hairline rules that only exist where they align content
options.viewport: Flush-left headline in the top-left fields; across the right columns the dependency graph assembles: scattered nodes snap onto grid intersections, edges route orthogonally, module fields fill in; the primary action sits flush-left under the headline.
options.risk: If a single grid line turns decorative it reads as one more dark developer page; every line must carry content.

raised.raise: Snap to module: parts may start far apart, but everything locks to one invisible module; the hero's reconstruction is that snap.
Focus reveal: any unit you focus grows and states what it is while everything else recedes.
One light: the accent is the only light in the scene and appears only on active architecture.
Linked propagation: one change visibly travels along every connected line.
Honest chrome: counts and labels sit small and exact on the element they describe.

options.label: Load Path
options.lineage: graphic statics and Gaudí's hanging-chain models
options.thesis: The architecture drawn as a structure under load: dependencies are forces, and the parts carrying the most weight are drawn heaviest.
materials: a hanging chain inverted into an arch
options.viewport: The dependency graph hangs from its entry points like a chain model; the heaviest components sag deepest, and inverting it shows the system's arch.
options.risk: Physics can overpromise precision; if the forces don't map to real measurements it becomes an engineering costume.

options.label: Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Architecture read like a mixing desk: every module a calibrated meter whose needle leans toward the red as structural pressure rises.
options.viewport: A row of identical meters across the top, one per module, settling as the analysis completes; the graph sits on the desk below.
options.case: Fuses well for Gravity, Entropy and risk readouts and speaks to engineers; loses on product clarity because structure, the product's core, is not a needle.
options.risk: Turns into a skeuomorphic gimmick unless every needle is a real measurement.

options.label: Modular Bars
options.lineage: modular identity systems of saturated bars
options.thesis: Loose parts thrown across the page snap into one loud modular grammar.
options.viewport: Bars and fragments scatter, then lock to the module around the headline.
options.case: Its snap mechanic fits, but the saturated palette breaks the brief's restraint and reads as an agency, not infrastructure.
options.kept: Snap to module: however far the parts are thrown, everything locks to one invisible module.
options.risk: Loud enough to bury the product.

options.label: Deployable Sheet
options.thesis: A compact packet that unfolds into the full crease graph in one pull.
options.viewport: A small packet in the corner unfolds across the viewport into a tessellated sheet.
options.case: Its propagation mechanic suits impact analysis, but a folded sheet hides nodes, edges and modules, and the paper palette breaks the brief.
options.kept: Linked propagation: one change visibly travels along every connected line.
options.risk: Beautiful, but about folding, not software.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles where the focused one grows and tells you what it is.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows of module tiles, one row lifted.
options.case: A wall of tiles hides the structure Katedrala exists to show.
options.kept: Focus reveal: the focused unit grows and states what it is while everything else recedes.

options.label: Indoor Sun
options.thesis: One vast hazed hall lit by a single amber light.
options.viewport: A half sun on the far wall completed by its reflection.
options.case: A mood, not a mechanism: it shows atmosphere, not architecture.
options.kept: One light: the accent is the only light in the scene.

options.label: Isometric Room
options.thesis: Identity as a small room you furnish.
options.viewport: A furnished room with counters and a guest ledger.
options.case: Personal and playful; developers evaluating infrastructure won't identify with it.
options.kept: Honest chrome: counts and labels sit small on the element they describe.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer-tool landing page, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and two buttons beside a product visual, feature rows below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every developer tool, by design.
